prompt: Build a Rectangle class with private fields, a constructor, getters, and area/perimeter methods. Complete the stubs in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A class bundles data (the private fields) with the methods that use that data -- this is encapsulation. Inside the constructor, this.width refers to the field while plain width refers to the parameter, so this.width = width copies the parameter into the object. Because area() and perimeter() are instance methods, they read the fields of whichever Rectangle object they are called on, which is why two different rectangles can report different areas.
hints: In the constructor, the parameter names shadow the fields; write this.width = width; and this.height = height;.
The getters simply return the corresponding field.
area() and perimeter() compute directly from the fields: width * height and 2 * (width + height).
